question.text: What is the capital city of Uruguay?

results.hint: Uruguay's largest city lies on the northern shore of the Río de la Plata estuary.
results.explanation: Montevideo is Uruguay’s largest city and its chief seaport.

question.text: In computer networking, what is meaning of the initials IP?

results.hint: It provides the addressing and routing rules that let data packets travel across interconnected networks.
results.explanation: Internet Protocol handles addressing and routing, while TCP often works alongside it to provide reliable, ordered delivery.

question.text: No Country for Old Men was released in which year?

results.hint: Its Best Picture win came at the 2008 Academy Awards, which honored films released the previous year.
results.explanation: No Country for Old Men was released in 2007 and went on to win four Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Supporting Actor for Javier Bardem.

question.text: Which author wrote 'Coriolanus'?

results.hint: The same playwright created Hamlet, Macbeth, and King Lear.
results.explanation: William Shakespeare based the tragedy on the Roman general Gaius Marcius Coriolanus, drawing on Plutarch's Lives.

incorrectAnswers: The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas

question.text: Which piece of written work starts with the line 'I will set down a tale as it was told to me by one who had it of his father, which latter had it of HIS father, this last having in like manner had it of HIS father—and so on, back and still back, three hundred years and more, the fathers transmitting it to the sons and so preserving it.'?

results.hint: Its author also created Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn.
results.explanation: The Prince and the Pauper imagines Edward VI and a poor London boy, Tom Canty, switching lives after discovering their resemblance.

question.text: What is the name of the white fox terrier owned by boy explorer Tintin?

results.hint: Tintin's canine companion is famously fond of whisky.
results.explanation: In the original French editions, Snowy is called Milou.

Which philosopher famously said 'The unexamined life is not worth living'?

results.hint: Plato records this saying in a defense speech delivered at a trial in Athens.
results.explanation: Plato's Apology recounts Socrates making this remark while defending his way of life before an Athenian jury.

question.text: Who shot President James Garfield?

results.hint: The assassin was a disappointed office seeker who believed he deserved a diplomatic post.
results.explanation: Charles Guiteau shot Garfield in 1881. Garfield survived for weeks before dying from infections related to his wounds and treatment.

question.text: What is the atomic number for thalium?

results.hint: On the periodic table, it comes immediately after mercury.

question.text: The Sixth Sense was released in which year?

results.hint: It shared its release year with The Matrix and Toy Story 2.
results.explanation: The Sixth Sense opened in 1999 and became famous for its twist ending and the line “I see dead people,” spoken by Haley Joel Osment’s character.

question.text: Which Canadian city takes its name from an Algonquin word meaning "to trade"?

results.hint: Canada's capital stands on the river that shares its name.
results.explanation: Ottawa was named after the Ottawa River; its name comes from an Algonquin word associated with trading.

question.text: What part of your body is the ischium a part of?

results.hint: It forms the lower, rear part of the hip bone and bears weight when you sit.
results.explanation: The ischium forms the lower, rear portion of each hip bone, and its prominent sitting surface is often called a sit bone.

question.text: What is the capital city of Costa Rica?

results.hint: Costa Rica's capital is in the Central Valley, a highland basin surrounded by volcanic mountains.
results.explanation: San José is also Costa Rica's largest city and its main political and economic center.

question.text: Who was the first boxer to defeat Lennox Lewis in a professional bout?

results.hint: His nickname was the Atomic Bull, and he stopped Lewis in the second round.
results.explanation: McCall stopped Lewis in the second round in 1994, winning the WBC heavyweight title.

question.text: What continent is the Bellingshausen Sea next to?

results.explanation: Antarctica borders the Bellingshausen Sea, which lies in the Southern Ocean west of the Antarctic Peninsula.

question.text: Which author wrote 'A Study in Scarlet'?

results.hint: The novel introduces Sherlock Holmes, the consulting detective who became one of literature’s most famous characters.
results.explanation: Arthur Conan Doyle introduced Dr. Watson alongside Holmes in this first Sherlock Holmes novel.

question.text: The XK120 was a model of car made by which manufacturer?

results.hint: The British marque is known for its leaping-cat emblem.
results.explanation: Jaguar named the XK120 for its advertised top speed of 120 mph; the car helped establish the company as a maker of high-performance sports cars.

question.text: The pasta casarecce has what meaning in Italian?

results.hint: Its name shares a root with the Italian word for “house.”
results.explanation: Casarecce comes from casereccio, meaning homemade. The short, twisted pasta has a groove that helps catch sauce.

question.text: What was the tax raised to pay off Viking raiders in Anglo-Saxon England called?

results.hint: Anglo-Saxon king Æthelred the Unready is closely associated with paying this tribute.
results.explanation: Danegeld was tribute paid to Viking raiders; its name combines an Old English word for payment with a term for the Danes.

question.text: Which actress has appeared in both Little Nicky and Walk the Line?

results.hint: She won an Oscar for playing country singer June Carter Cash.
results.explanation: Reese Witherspoon won the Academy Award for Best Actress for portraying June Carter Cash in Walk the Line.

question.text: What term is used to describe an item that's sold at retail for less than it cost wholesale as a way to lure customers?

results.hint: Retailers may price a staple unusually low, hoping shoppers also buy higher-margin goods.
results.explanation: A loss leader is priced below the retailer’s cost to attract customers, who may then purchase other, more profitable items.

question.text: Which of these countries borders Zimbabwe?

results.hint: Zimbabwe's western neighbor has Gaborone as its capital.
results.explanation: Botswana is home to much of the Okavango Delta, a vast inland wetland known for its wildlife.

question.text: The painting "Portrait de L’artiste Sans Barbe" by Vincent van Gogh is a part of which art movement?

results.hint: Van Gogh, Gauguin, and Cézanne are all closely associated with this late-19th-century movement.
results.explanation: Post-Impressionism covers varied approaches that moved beyond the effects of light and color emphasized by Impressionist painters. Van Gogh is one of its best-known artists.

question.text: Who won the 2012 Academy Award for Best Leading Actor for playing the role of Abraham Lincoln in Lincoln?

results.hint: He became the first man to win three Academy Awards for Best Actor.
results.explanation: Daniel Day-Lewis's earlier Best Actor wins were for My Left Foot and There Will Be Blood.

question.text: Which rock band's fourth album had no title or name on the cover, but sold millions of copies?

results.hint: Its singer was Robert Plant, and its guitarist was Jimmy Page.
results.explanation: The untitled album is commonly called Led Zeppelin IV and includes “Stairway to Heaven.”

question.text: Which philosopher famously said 'The function of prayer is not to influence God, but rather to change the nature of the one who prays'?

results.hint: This Danish thinker is often regarded as a forerunner of existentialism.
results.explanation: Søren Kierkegaard’s writings explored faith and inwardness, themes reflected in the idea that prayer transforms the person who prays.

question.text: Which author wrote 'The Phantom of the Opera'?

results.hint: The French journalist behind this novel also wrote The Mystery of the Yellow Room.
results.explanation: Gaston Leroux was a French journalist as well as a novelist. He first published The Phantom of the Opera as a newspaper serial.

question.text: Which English rock band released the album 'The Piper at the Gates of Dawn'?

results.hint: Its early lineup included guitarist and singer Syd Barrett.
results.explanation: Pink Floyd took the album title from a chapter in Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows.

question.text: Which actor has featured in roles including 30 Rock and The Departed?

results.hint: On 30 Rock, he played the network executive Jack Donaghy.
results.explanation: Alec Baldwin played network executive Jack Donaghy on 30 Rock and Captain Ellerby in The Departed.
